title: How to Watch the Chiefs vs. Colts Live Online
description:

body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs return to primetime Sunday night for a Week 2 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts, with the game airing nationally on NBC and streaming live on Peacock.

	The Chiefs host the Colts at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, Sept. 20, with kickoff set for 8:20 p.m. ET. NBC’s coverage begins an hour earlier with “Football Night in America” at 7 p.m. ET. The game will also be available to stream live through a variety of Live TV streamers such as Sling TV, DirecTV, Fubo TV and Hulu + Live TV.


	Sling TV subscribers can watch Chiefs vs. Colts through NBC in select markets with a Sling Blue-based plan. For football fans looking beyond a single game, Sling is currently offering a five-month Season Pass, including Blue + Sports Extra for $234 prepaid. The bundle adds channels such as NFL RedZone and NFL Network, while NBC is available through Sling Blue in supported markets.

	Kansas City enters Sunday’s matchup at 1-0 after beating the Denver Broncos 31-10 in its season opener. Mahomes threw for 173 yards and two touchdowns while adding another score on the ground, while new Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III made an immediate impact with 173 rushing yards and two total touchdowns. Travis Kelce added a game-high 71 receiving yards.

	Indianapolis, meanwhile, is looking to bounce back from a 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens. Daniel Jones threw for 166 yards and a touchdown in his return from last season’s Achilles injury, while Jonathan Taylor finished with 121 yards from scrimmage and two rushing touchdowns.


	Stream the Chiefs vs. Colts live online on Sling TV here.

title: Aaron Sorkin Says Jeremy Strong Treated His Co-Stars ‘The Way He Imagines’ Mark Zuckerberg Treats People While Shooting ‘The Social Reckoning’
description: Director Aaron Sorkin told The New York Times in the latest edition of The Interview that his “Social Reckoning” star Jeremy Strong, a known method
body:
Director Aaron Sorkin told The New York Times in the latest edition of The Interview that his “Social Reckoning” star Jeremy Strong, a known method actor, was treating his co-stars “the way he imagines” Mark Zuckerberg would treat them during filming. Strong, of course, plays the Meta CEO in “The Social Network” follow-up.

	“Jeremy does a lot of his own work. He does a tremendous amount of work before he shows up on your set,” Sorkin said. “He did not speak in his own voice on the set or walk the way Jeremy walks.”
	

	He continued, “I told all the other actors in his scenes: ‘Guys, he’s not going to be hanging out with you at craft service. He’s not going to be yucking it up with you between takes. He’s probably not going to speak to you at all. He is going to treat you the way he imagines Mark treats the people around him.’ And that’s what happened. You cannot argue with the results.”

	Jeremy Allen White, Mikey Madison. Bill Burr, Betty Gilpin and Billy Magnussen star alongside Strong in “The Social Reckoning,” which follows whistleblower Frances Haugen, who teams up with Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz to expose the sinister inner workings of Zuckerberg’s Facebook.

	Despite turbulence with the rollout of other tech dramas like the OpenAI expose “Artificial,” Sorkin explained there has been no such trouble with “The Social Reckoning.” He said that reps for Meta reached out asking for tickets to see the film.

	“It’s my understanding that Sony did get letters from Meta, and I do not think those letters said: ‘We’re wishing you all the luck in the world. Send us some tickets for opening night,’” Sorkin said. “Under ordinary circumstances, with a piece of nonfiction, the studio’s legal department would do a thorough vet. With this movie, they hired an outside law firm just to handle the legal vet to make sure that every single thing that is presented as a fact is a fact.”
	

	“The Social Reckoning” hits theaters on Oct. 9.

schema.headline: Aaron Sorkin Says Jeremy Strong Treated His Co-Stars ‘The Way He Imagines’ Mark Zuckerberg Treats People While Shooting ‘The Social Reckoning’

title: ‘La Bola Negra’ Takes 2026 TIFF Audience Award
description: The generational queer drama “La Bola Negra” has taken the 2026 TIFF People’s Choice Award, a coveted audience prize out of the annual film festival
body:
The generational queer drama “La Bola Negra” has taken the 2026 TIFF People’s Choice Award, a coveted audience prize out of the annual film festival in Toronto. 

	Directed by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, the Netflix project has been on a tear since world premiering in Cannes this year (where it earned a 16-minute standing ovation and won best director for the pair known as “Los Javis”). The film is described as an epic about “the lives of three men intertwined in love and loss across eras.”
	

	The audience award is largely seen as an indicator of legs on the road to the Oscars stage. “La Bola” edged out first-runner-up “I Play Rocky,” Peter Farrelly’s crowd-pleaser about the making of the Sylvester Stallone classic. Siân Heder’s Apple project, “Being Heumann,” came in as the second runner-up.


	The People’s Choice Documentary Award went to “Darlene Love: I Know Where I’ve Been.” Director Barry Avirch examines the life and impact of Love, who spent “many years she spent providing lead and background vocals, often uncredited, for some of the biggest hits of the 1960s while under contract to Phil Spector, the superstar producer who became her nemesis.” The film features interviews with Dionne Warwick, Bruce Springsteen, and David Letterman. The doc category’s first runner-up was James Marcus Haney’s “Black Sunflowers,” followed by Mila Aung-Thwin’s “The Ultra Runner.”

	“Elsinore” won the TIFF International People’s Choice Award. Director Simon Stone called the Andrew Scott vehicle “a celebration of life. Of choosing courage and creativity in the face of great challenges,” and a “love letter to actors and artists everywhere … those who give themselves fully to their craft.” Lee Chang-dong’s “Possible Love” came in as first runner-up with Hur Jin-ho “The Assassin(s)” at second.
	

	Finally, the People’s Choice Midnight Madness Award went to “Ladies and Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney.” Director Matthew Rankin’s archival clip show of Canada’s 18th Prime Minister has been praised as both an arty multimedia exploration and the “weirdest” film at TIFF this year. Paolo Strippoli’s “The Spiral” came in as first runner-up, with Sabu’s “Arrested Memory” in second.

schema.headline: ‘La Bola Negra’ Takes 2026 TIFF Audience Award

title: Kate Beckinsale Posts Cryptic Messages on Social Media, Sparking Concern from Fans
description:
“Serendipity” actor Kate Beckinsale posted cryptic messages to her personal social media account early Sunday morning, leaving fans concerned. 

	Be
body:
“Serendipity” actor Kate Beckinsale posted cryptic messages to her personal social media account early Sunday morning, leaving fans concerned. 

	Beckinsale posted a black screen with “bye” written across it on her Instagram story, followed by a second post of a rainbow with the text “congratulations you won i give up.” These posts have since been deleted, but were reposted by worried fans on X. She currently has no posts on Instagram.
	

	Reps for Beckinsale did not immediately respond to Variety’s request for comment.


	The actress has a history of taking to social media to air her grievances. In a since-deleted Instagram video from earlier in September, Beckinsale said that “people have seen or experienced levels of horror, terror, violence” don’t “just dream about incessantly, so there’s no rest. They see it when they blink. Every time they close their eyes for a second and those people aren’t recognized as heroes.”

	“Given the fact that it’s invisible and you can’t know, maybe err on being on the gentler side with people, being kinder with people,” she added at the time. “It really is true that if you haven’t walked a mile in someone’s shoes — however fancy you feel the shoes are — you have absolutely no idea what they may be carrying or masking or dealing with day and night.”

	After her mother Judy Loe’s death in July 2025 after a battle with stage IV cancer, Beckinsale discussed her struggles online. People reported that she previously shared on her Instagram dozens of negative comments she’s received about her appearance amid her grief.
	

	If you or anyone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline by dialing 988 or go to SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

schema.headline: Kate Beckinsale Posts Cryptic Messages on Social Media, Sparking Concern from Fans

title: ‘Though I Am an Inept Villainess’ Adds New Cast Ahead of January 2027 Return
description: Toho Co., Ltd. has unveiled new cast additions and a key visual for the second cour of its TV anime “Though I Am an Inept Villainess,” subtitled “Th
body:
Toho Co., Ltd. has unveiled new cast additions and a key visual for the second cour of its TV anime “Though I Am an Inept Villainess,” subtitled “The First Royal Outing” Arc, ahead of the show’s January 2027 return. 

	In Japanese television, a cour refers to a broadcast block of roughly three months, and anime seasons are often split into multiple cours that air separately rather than airing all at once.


	Nakamura Yuichi will voice Keikou, the eldest brother of lead character Reirin, while Toki Shunichi takes on the role of Keishou, her second-eldest brother. Kobayashi Chiaki joins as Unran, a young village chief from the south whose role expands as the plot moves forward. 
	

	“Though I Am an Inept Villainess” is based on Nakamura Satsuki’s light novel series and premiered as a TV anime in July 2026. The story follows Reirin, whose ordinary life unravels after Keigetsu, shunned by her peers, turns to banned sorcery to trade their bodies, leaving each woman to cope with the other’s world. The anime’s first part closed with the disturbances tied to the body-swap curse largely resolved, and with Reirin and Keigetsu having grown closer after coming to understand each other through the experience.

	The new arc picks up in early fall, as the Shu clan’s southern territory prepares to host the Harvest Festival, a ritual in which the Crown Prince and the Maidens pray for a plentiful harvest. Keigetsu presses ahead with preparations despite lacking a consort as guardian, while Reirin backs her efforts and looks forward to her first outing in a royal capacity.

	Trouble strikes soon after the pair arrive for the ceremony. An accident disrupts the ritual, and Keigetsu, thrown off balance, sees her spell spiral out of her control, sending the two women back into each other’s bodies. In the chaos that follows, Reirin is abducted. Her brothers Kou Keikou and Kou Keishou step in as the search for an unidentified figure framing Keigetsu unfolds.
	

	“The First Royal Outing” Arc is set to begin streaming in January 2027, though Toho has not yet confirmed an exact premiere date. 

	Earlier in the series, maidens representing the Five Clans competed for the Crown Prince’s affection, a rivalry that pushed a jealous Keigetsu to resort to banned sorcery and trade places with the popular Reirin. The swap gave Keigetsu no advantage, since she took on a frail body already near death, while Reirin, saddled with Keigetsu’s tarnished name, stood trial for wrongdoing she had no part in.

schema.headline: ‘Though I Am an Inept Villainess’ Adds New Cast Ahead of January 2027 Return

title: Sylvester Stallone Says He Turned Down Trump’s ‘Special Ambassador’ to Hollywood Role Because It Was ‘Impossible’: ‘I Said Thank You and Ciao’
description: Sylvester Stallone may hold the Trump-bestowed title of “special ambassador” to Hollywood, but nearly two years since his appointment, the “Rocky” a
body:
Sylvester Stallone may hold the Trump-bestowed title of “special ambassador” to Hollywood, but nearly two years since his appointment, the “Rocky” actor has divulged that he didn’t explicitly sign up for the role.

	“Well, it just happened,” the Oscar nominee noted in a recent interview with The Sunday Times. “I was watching TV one night and they go, ‘So Stallone and Mel Gibson and Jon Voight will be …’ And I went, ‘What?’ I said, ‘Excuse me? Really?’ Because if they had asked me in the beginning, I would have said, this is not possible.”
	

	The star continued to open up about his reservations surrounding the appointment, and if he was hesitant: “Yes, because Hollywood, I guess it’s like feudal states. They have their little kingdoms. You don’t go in and tell six studios how to do things. And Mel Gibson and Jon Voight, we’re kind of do-our-own-thing people.”


	He even recalled telling Trump that “it won’t work.” “I said thank you and ciao, because it’s impossible. Hollywood works, and it will evolve. It’s corporate and corporate people won’t want to hear me tell them about finance.” 

	Stallone, Gibson and Voight were first announced as “special ambassadors” by the current president in Jan. 2025 when he shared the following statement on Truth Social: “It is my honor to announce Jon Voight, Mel Gibson, and Sylvester Stallone, to be Special Ambassadors to a great but very troubled place, Hollywood, California. They will serve as Special Envoys to me for the purpose of bringing Hollywood, which has lost much business over the last four years to Foreign Countries, BACK—BIGGER, BETTER, AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE! These three very talented people will be my eyes and ears, and I will get done what they suggest. It will again be, like The United States of America itself, The Golden Age of Hollywood!”
	

	Despite Stallone’s initial feelings about the appointment, the actor still speaks fondly of Trump. In the interview, Stallone noted that he introduced the president-elect as a “mythical character” when at a party at Mar-a-Lago. “Nobody in the world could’ve pulled off what he pulled off, so I’m in awe,” he said.

schema.headline: Sylvester Stallone Says He Turned Down Trump’s ‘Special Ambassador’ to Hollywood Role Because It Was ‘Impossible’: ‘I Said Thank You and Ciao’

title: Edward Morris, Nashville Music Editor and Columnist Who Steered Billboard’s Country Coverage, Dies at 90
description: Edward Morris, a Nashville-based music journalist who edited Billboard‘s country coverage, wrote a popular CMT.com column and penned numerous books,
body:
Edward Morris, a Nashville-based music journalist who edited Billboard‘s country coverage, wrote a popular CMT.com column and penned numerous books, died Thursday at age 90. The family did not give a cause of death.

	Morris was best remembered in the country community for a 14-year tenure with Billboard from 1981 to 1995, the last four of those as the publication’s country music editor. Prior to coming on staff, his contributions to Billboard as a freelancer dated back to 1972.
	

	In 1999, he joined CMT.com as a writer, where his byline continued to enjoy prominence in the country community. The website became the primary go-to for consumers looking for country news, and Morris remained there into his mid-80s, until 2020, when, under cover of COVID, MTV Networks began to dismantle its once-flourishing news sites.


	His eight books included “Edward Morris’ Complete Guide To Country Music Videos” (1997), “Garth Brooks: Platinum Cowboy” (1993), “Alabama” (1985), “At Carter’s Stanley’s Grave: Musings on Country Music & Musicians” (2011), and “Scorched Mirth and Acid Reflux” (2019). He also wrote liner notes for releases by the Judds, Keith Whitley, Guy Clark, Eddy Arnold, Hank Snow and Chet Atkins, among others.

	In 2002, Morris was honored at Belmont University’s annual International Country Music Conference (ICMC) with its Charlie Lamb Journalist of the Year award.

	In addition to Billboard and CMT.com, Morris’ articles were published in the Journal of Country Music, Advertising Age, TV Guide, McCall’s, the Hollywood Reporter, Amusement Business, Book Page, Mother Earth News, Bluegrass Unlimited and the Saturday Evening Post. Since turning 90, he had begun writing a column for his local paper, the Kingston Springs Gazette.
	

	Morris was married to another boldface name in Nashville, veteran country music publicist Norma Morris, who died in 2021 (read her Variety obituary here). He wrote a book about the final evolution of his relationship with Norma, “Stardust: An Alzheimer’s Love Story,” which stemmed from blogs and social posts he had written about their journey as they fell apart and then came together again as she required intensive care.

	In a 2023 interview with the website FiftyForward, Morris said, “I like words… I listen to words, listen to people talk, listen to cliches. The inspiration is just everywhere. I sort of see writing as a performance. You know, you hear musicians say that they would do it for free if they weren’t paid for it. And I feel the same way about writing. I love to write with the anticipation of amusing people or getting arguments started or whatever.”

	Morris recalled aspects of his career for the site. Asked about highlights of being a country music journalist, he answered, “The first one was that I was able to meet the Grand Ole Opry stars that I’d listened to as a boy, and to meet Ernest Tubb, Roy Acuff, Pee Wee King, Eddy Arnold and Minnie Pearl, even Herman Crook of the Crook Brothers, who was one of the original acts of the Opry. That was a big deal for me, probably more than even meeting the contemporary country stars, because I met them sort of on a business-like basis. But the others, I just stood in adoration.”

	He called his two decades with CMT “the easiest job I’ve ever had. All I had to do was just cover country music and especially the No. 1 parties. And so, in my 20 years with CMT, I don’t think I was in their office more than five times. I worked from home, and I got to see the internal gears of the music industry, and virtually anything that I wanted to cover, they let me cover. So, I was always out at events and parties and award shows and all that. And, as I say, you get to appreciate the backstage part of the industry when you have a job like that.”

	Talking about his “Stardust” book, Morris recalled how he had once reviewed a book on Alzheimer’s as a book critic, and said, “This was long before Norma showed any signs. As I read the book it was almost like being beset by claustrophobia. It seemed like it must be the worst fate in the world to have Alzheimer’s. I was surprised — although I’m sure it was the worst fate for Norma — I was surprised that being able to write about it seemed to me to let a little light in. … And I wanted to make one point clear. Sometimes the caregiver comes out as some kind of heroic figure. I was not that. All my family, all my three children and six grandchildren, and five great-grandchildren live here in Nashville. I had all sorts of help taking care of Norma. So it wasn’t, you know, me against the world or anything like that. But there were great moments in an otherwise tragic story.”
	

	Morris also stretched his wings in later years to become a playwright. In 2016, at 80, he wrote his first stage production, “The Passion of Ethel Rosenberg,” a one-woman play that was said to reflect his “lifelong support of leftist political causes.” It was produced in Nashville and Sante Fe and had a public reading at New York’s Museum of Jewish Heritage. 

	Ed Morris is survived by daughters Erin Morris Huttlinger and Rachel Serrato, and by son Jason Morris. Their brother, Christopher, died at age 2. He is also survived by six grandchildren and seven great-grandchildren. 

	In lieu of flowers, the family suggests that donations cbe made to Planned Parenthood.

schema.headline: Edward Morris, Nashville Music Editor and Columnist Who Steered Billboard’s Country Coverage, Dies at 90

title: ‘La Bola Negra’ Producer Movistar Plus Unveils Projects from ‘The Good Boss’ Director Fernando León, J.A. Bayona, Los Moriarti
description: Movistar Plus, producer of “La Bola Negra,” “The Beloved” and “Sirāt ” has unveiled a new slate of projects headed by titles from “The Good Boss” di
body:
Movistar Plus, producer of “La Bola Negra,” “The Beloved” and “Sirāt ” has unveiled a new slate of projects headed by titles from “The Good Boss” director Fernando León, director-producer JA Bayona (“Society of the Snow”) and actor-director Paco Leon (“Arde Madrid”).

	Further projects are set to be directed by Los Moriarti (“The Endless Trench”), Daniel Monzón (“Cell 211”), Sandra Romero (“Where the Silence Passes”) and Cristóbal Garrido and Adolfo Valor (“La vida breve”).
	

	The new slate marks the first under new Movistar Plus CEO Alfonso Gómez Palacio, made in his first public appearance, flanked by Juan Andrés García Romero “Bropi,” who took up the position of Movistar Plus director of contents in May.


	It came as Garcia Ropero announced that Movistar Plus would bow a new Spanish film every week of the year.

	Added to an earlier announcement in July, where Movistar Plus committed to doubling its annual number of Spanish original series from eight to 16, the new strategy unveil reconfirms its aim to step up and broaden Spanish film-TV production, co-production and acquisitions.

	“We want Movistar Plus to be the most relevant platform for our clients and Spain’s audiovisual industry,” Gómez Palacio said Sunday at the San Sebastián Film Festival where the presentation was made.

	He added: “Our ambition is to grow through contents, supporting talent, diving new projects in Spanish with a unique vision offering propositions which nobody else can offer: the best original production alongside big international streaming services and the best sports offer.
	

	More new film-TV project details:

	*“La Náufraga,” created, written and directed by Fernando León de Aranoa is an exclusive Movistar Plus series producida por Jaume Roures, León de Aranoa y Patricia de Muns. Ir stars Belén Cuesta, just seen at San Sebastián in “5 More Minutes.”

	*JA Bayona will executive produce two new non-fiction projects.

	*The Moriarty, (“Marco,” “The Endless Trench”) will direct a fiction project, “with the stamp of Carles Porta,” one of Spain’s masters of true crime, with a tony Spanish star cast of Anna Castillo, Pol López and Eduard Fernández.

	*Daniel Monzón is set to direct “250 Metros,” a Movistar Plus original film produced with Edmon Roch’s Ikiru Films and Basoilarraren, starring Luis Tosar and written by longtime Monzón and Alex de la Iglesia co-scribe Jorge Guerricaechevarría.

	*Another Movistar Plus original, the movie “Una visita familiar,” is set to be produced by Mammut, Icónica Producciones and Bteam Prods, and directed by Sandra Romero, also a helmer on “Many People Need to Die,” Movistar Plus’ biggest Spanish series of 2026.

	*Cristóbal Garrido and Adolfo Valor are preparing a comedy starring David Verdaguer and Paula Malia.

	*Co-creator, co-writer, director and star of “Arde Madrid,” one of the biggest breakouts in Movistar Plus’ now 10 years of productions, Paco León, famed for his performances in “Aida” and “The House of Flowers,” is described as having “a project” set up in development at Movistar Plus.

	“We’d like to listen more, work with more talent and open the door to more stories. Spain’s industry is living an extraordinary moment and we believe that Movistar Plus has the responsibility to contribute to its continued growth, We’re looking for projects with quality, personality and their own vision. We want stories which nobody else dares to tell,” said Juan Andrés García Ropero “Bropi.”

	More to come.

schema.headline: ‘La Bola Negra’ Producer Movistar Plus Unveils Projects from ‘The Good Boss’ Director Fernando León, J.A. Bayona, Los Moriarti

title: NFL’s 20 Hottest WAGs: Taylor Swift, Madison Beer, Normani and More
description:
Sep 20, 2026 10:00am PT	
	


	A term previously used to describe the wives of girlfriends of footballers across the pond has travele
body:
Sep 20, 2026 10:00am PT	
	


	A term previously used to describe the wives of girlfriends of footballers across the pond has traveled to America’s most popular sport.
	
			


			
			
	

									2025 iHeartMedia / Dimitrios Kambouris / Astrid Stawiarz
	

		
	
				

	The term WAGs (wives and girlfriends) was popularized by the U.K. press in the early aughts in relation to Victoria Beckham, a pop singer for the Spice Girls who was married to star footballer David Beckham and a frequent fixture at his matches. While originally referring to the wives and girlfriends of footballers across the pond, and meant to be a tad reductive, it’s now been adopted as part of the cultural lexicon and has made its way to America’s most popular sport: football.

	The coupling of Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce, the pop superstar and stud tight end for the NFL’s Kansas City Chiefs (who now makes considerable more money off the field via his podcast and brand deals), has put the NFL’s WAGs under the spotlight. Swift almost single-handedly increased the NFL’s popularity among girls and women, including a 53% increase among girls aged 12-17 and 34% increase in women 35+, while adding an estimated $1 billion+ in revenue to the league.

	And the NFL took notice. Prior to this season, the league highlighted its WAGs like pop star Madison Beer (fiancée of Chargers QB Justin Herbert), model Olivia Ponton (girlfriend of Bengals QB Joe Burrow) and influencer Marissa Ayers (Giants QB Jaxson Dart’s partner) by capturing footage of them getting cozy with their significant others at NFL training camp as part of a coordinated content rollout.

	And so, with the spotlight shining on them brighter than ever and the NFL season in full swing, here are the NFL’s top WAGs, which range from influencers (and lots of them) to pop stars, entrepreneurs and Olympic gold medalists.


			
			
	Taylor Swift
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for The Recording A				
					
				
	“Your English teacher and your gym teacher are getting married.” That was how Swift, the most famous and awarded musician on the planet, announced her engagement to Kelce, the future Hall of Fame tight end (and three-time NFL champion) for the Kansas City Chiefs. Swift single-handedly helped improve the NFL’s popularity among women when she started dating Kelce and showing up to Chief games, increasing NFL viewership among teen girls by 53% while generating over $1 billion in value for the league. Swift and Kelce, of course, are now husband and wife, having tied the knot in July in a star-studded ceremony at New York City’s Madison Square Garden.
		
			
			
	Madison Beer
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for Victoria's Secr				
					
				
	Madison Beer is the latest pop star to generate headlines with an NFL boyfriend. Dating rumors sparked in Aug. 2025 after Los Angeles Chargers QB Justin Herbert was pictured on the set of one of her music videos. She went on to attend several Chargers games, and their relationship was confirmed in October as they sat courtside at a Lakers game. The couple got engaged in July, and Beer shared a carousel of photos via Instagram captioned, “meet my fiancé.” In Jan. 2025, Beer released her third studio album, “Locket,” featuring fan favorites “Yes Baby” and “Bittersweet.” There’s no word on new music just yet, and it seems the couple has turned their attention towards two things: football and planning a wedding.
		
			
			
	Hailee Steinfeld
			
										
					Image Credit: Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images				
					
				
	Actress Hailee Steinfeld burst onto screens as plucky farm girl Mattie Ross in the Coen brothers’ 2010 film “True Grit,” earning an Oscar nomination for her breakthrough performance. She’s made quite a name for herself since, starring in a slew of films, including “The Edge of Seventeen” and her scene-stealing turn in “Sinners.” She also briefly moonlighted as a pop star — and was a member of Taylor Swift’s once-legendary posse in the “Bad Blood” music video. She began dating Buffalo Bills quarterback (and 2024 league MVP) Josh Allen in 2023, and the pair tied the knot in May 2025. Earlier this year, they welcomed a baby girl named Harper; Allen described her as “the most unbelievable blessing.”
		
			
			
	Normani
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for MTV/ViacomCBS				
					
				
	The former member of popular girl group Fifth Harmony, of “Work from Home” fame, caused quite the stir with her debut solo single “Motivation” (and accompanying dance-heavy music video). She released her long-awaited debut album “Dopamine” in 2024, recently served as a guest judge on “America’s Got Talent” and has been dating the Pittsburgh Steelers’ muscle-bound wide receiver DK Metcalf, a two-time Pro Bowl selection, since 2022. Metcalf announced the couple’s engagement in March 2025 during his introductory press conference upon joining the Steelers.
		
			
			
	Simone Biles
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for TIME				
					
				
	Simone Biles needs no introduction. Born in Ohio and raised in Texas, the 7-time Olympic gold medalist made her Olympic debut during the 2016 games in Rio. Her husband, safety Jonathan Owens, was a free agent following the end of his contract with the Chicago Bears, and in March signed on to the Indianapolis Colts. The couple first made headlines three years ago, when Owens shared that they’d met on a dating app but alleged he’d had no idea who Biles was, elsewhere implying that he was “a catch.” The pair have been married since April 2023.
		
			
			
	Olivia Culpo
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for Victoria's Secr				
					
				
	The beauty pageant game was Olivia Culpo’s first claim to fame, having won both Miss Rhode Island USA and Miss USA in 2012. As social media began to take over, she pivoted and pursued a career as an influencer. Prior to meeting her now-husband Christian McCaffrey — Pro Bowl running back for the San Francisco 49ers and son of wide receiver Ed McCaffrey — she was in a two-year relationship with Nick Jonas, even starring in the music video for “Jealous.” Now, she and McCaffrey have a baby girl, Colette, with another child on the way. In July, she launched Picolette, described as “an elevated baby collection,” in collaboration with Target.
		
			
			
	Chloe Kim
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for TIME				
					
				
	The 26-year-old two-time Olympic champion snowboarder became the youngest woman ever to capture Olympic gold as a 17-year-old, and has three gold medals at the World Championships as well as five ESPY Awards. A second-generation Korean-American, Kim’s father moved to America with only $800 in his pocket and made his way, eventually quitting his job to fully support Kim’s blossoming snowboarding career. Kim began dating All-Pro defensive end Myles Garrett of the Los Angeles Rams in 2025 and the two are still going strong.
		
			
			
	Brittany Mahomes
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				
	Brittany Mahomes, wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, has been with her husband from the start. They met and started dating while in high school, and Mahomes popped the question eight years later in 2020. The special moment took place at Arrowhead Stadium, on the same day as the ring ceremony for Super Bowl LIV. That same year she became a partial owner of Kansas City National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL), now named the Kansas City Current. She’s also landed several brand deals and partnerships with Amazon, Adidas and Whoop. Fellow Chiefs WAG Taylor Swift has even buddied up with Mahomes, and the duo often sit together at games when Swift is in attendance.
		
			
			
	Olivia Ponton
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for Universal Pictu				
					
				
	Influencer and book podcaster Olivia Ponton is a WAG shrouded in mystery. The 24-year-old was first linked to Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow in 2024 when she called to report a burglary at Burrow’s Ohio home that had occurred while the team was in Dallas playing the Cowboys. Since then, she and Burrow have had only a handful of public appearances, the most recent during Bengals training camp in August. The pair have neither confirmed nor denied their relationship. Her podcast, “Booked, Blonde & Busy,” is in the middle of its second season, with guests including “Sex and the City” writer Candace Bushnell.
		
			
			
	Marissa Ayers
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for White Fox				
					
				
	Ayers is a social media influencer 1.6 million TikTok follower, model and ring girl for Jake Paul’s boxing company MVP Promotions. And she may be a graduate of the University of Alabama, but she’s dating former Ole Miss quarterback (and current New York Giants rising star) Jaxson Dart, aka Donald Trump’s favorite QB. Ayers confirmed the couple’s relationship in Jan. 2026 and they subsequently made their red carpet debut in February at 2026 NFL Honors.
		
			
			
	Haley Cavinder
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for Sports Illustrated				
					
				
	Haley (on the left), along with her fraternal twin Hanna, make up the Cavinder Twins, former college basketball players for the Miami Hurricanes turned social media stars. The sisters have 4.5 million TikTok followers, netted millions in NIL deals while in school, are official brand ambassadors for Under Armour and co-founded the clothing company Baseline Team. Cavinder has been with Dallas Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson since 2023, and the two lovebirds got married on June 20, 2026, in Miami.
		
			
			
	Sydney Warner
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for Revlon				
					
				
	There are plenty of influencer gals amongst NFL WAGs, and Warner is one of them, amassing 3.5 million TikTok followers. She also appeared as a contestant on Season 24 of ABC’s reality-dating competition “The Bachelor.” While she may not have been Peter Weber’s choice in the end, her appearance on the show led Pro Bowl linebacker Fred Warner of the San Francisco 49ers to slide into her DMs. The two got married in 2022 and welcomed their second child together in January of this year.
		
			
			
	Anna Hall Slayton
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				
	Simone Biles and Chloe Kim aren’t the only Olympians to make the list. Slayton, 25, is the reigning heptathlon world champion and won two NCAA Division 1 titles while at the University of Florida. At the end of last year, she got engaged to wide receiver Darius Slayton, and the couple got married in April. Just weeks ago, however, the news broke that Slayton had been released by the New York Giants and is now a free agent. It was a change that many saw coming, and the player has yet to be acquired by another team. His other half, meanwhile, continues to train and compete in her own sport under her professional contract with Adidas.
		
			
			
	Anna Congdon
			
										
					Image Credit: Instagram				
					
				
	Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley met his girlfriend Anna Congdon while the two attended Penn State in 2016. They have two children together, Jada and Saquon, born in April 2018 and Sept. 2022, respectively. In 2025, Barkley proposed to his longtime partner just weeks ahead of the Eagles’ Super Bowl appearance against the Kansas City Chiefs, and that October, the entire family featured in the documentary “Saquon” from Prime Video.
		
			
			
	Mahogany Jones
			
										
					Image Credit: Instagram				
					
				
	Deebo Samuel has lit up the NFL as a wide receiver (and occasional running back) since 2019, earning All-Pro honors in 2021, and Jones has been by his side through all of it. The couple has remained extremely private, but fans were offered a rare glimpse into their life through “The Deebo Samuel Documentary” where she briefly – but warmly – talks about her life with Samuel and raising a child together. Samuel is currently a wide receiver for the San Francisco 49ers and yes, his nickname comes from Tiny Lister Jr.’s character in the movie “Friday.”
		
			
			
	Kristin Juszczyk
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for Fanatics				
					
				
	On Jan. 14, 2024, Taylor Swift showed up to a Chiefs game sporting a puffer jacket that sent fans into a frenzy. Later, via Instagram, Juszczyk confirmed she had created Swift’s jacket and shared a behind-the-scenes look at her creative process. Later that same month, she got the coveted NFL licensing rights, leading to the launch of her brand Off Season, which operates under the Fanatics umbrella. She is married to Kyle Juszczyk, who’s been a fullback for the San Francisco 49ers since 2017. In August, Off Season rolled out its newest NFL collection with a campaign starring WAGs from the Detroit Lions, Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots.
		
			
			
	Ronika Stone Love
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				
	The California native is the daughter of former NFL guard Ron Stone and was a volleyball star while at the University of Oregon, ranking third in total blocks and fifth in points, and later went pro with San Diego Pro Volleyball. Love has dated Green Bay Packers QB Jordan Love since September 2020, when the two linked up during the pandemic, and has gone viral a number of times on TikTok (where she has 250K followers) sharing content of the eye-catching couple. They got married in 2025 and welcomed their first child together in May 2026.
		
			
			
	Christen Harper Goff
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for Sports Illustra				
					
				
	Christen and Jared Goff are a Raya success story. The couple met in 2018 while he was playing for the Los Angeles Rams. He would remain with the team through the end of the 2020 season, and in 2021 was traded to the Detroit Lions. Her career is a combination of acting, modeling, and influencer work. She has been featured in every Sports Illustrated issue since 2022 after winning the brand’s Swim Search competition the year prior, and walked in one of its famed runway shows earlier this year. In 2025, the couple welcomed their first child, Romy, who joined Harper Goff in cheering on from the sidelines.
		
			
			
	Claire Kittle
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				
	Kittle first met her husband George, an elite tight end for the San Francisco 49ers, when the two were freshmen at the University of Iowa back in 2012. But Kittle is an athlete in her own right — a former McDonald’s All-American basketball player who played for the Iowa Hawkeyes in college before a knee injury sidelined her. The two tied the knot in 2019, and now Kittle, who competed in bikini competitions, runs her own training company, Claire Till Fitness, and broadcasts content to her 500K Instagram followers.
		
			
			
	Hannah Brooke Johnson
			
										
					Image Credit: Netflix				
					
				
	If Johnson looks familiar at all, it’s because she was a contestant of Season 5 of Netflix’s addictive reality-dating series “Too Hot to Handle.” The model, reality star and influencer met defensive end Jermaine Johnson II at a Super Bowl event in 2023, and he proposed two years later. The couple got married in July in Laguna Beach, California, surrounded by family, friends and plenty of athletes and reality stars. Johnson II, a former Pro Bowler for the Jets, currently plays for the Tennessee Titans.

title: From Oprah Winfrey and Christopher Nolan to Kim Kardashian and Robert De Niro: Inside the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art Opening Gala
description: During her introductory remarks at the opening of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art on Saturday night, Mellody Hobson said her husband, famed “Star Wa
body:
During her introductory remarks at the opening of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art on Saturday night, Mellody Hobson said her husband, famed “Star Wars” director George Lucas, was nervous about the evening’s turnout.
“This room is filled with our friends,” Hobson said. “Looking out at your faces, you have no idea how much you mean to us, how much you mean to us in every way. George kept saying, ‘Will this person come? Do you think that person will come?’ I said, ‘They will all come, George.’”
And come they did.
The powerhouse crowd was a melting pot of Hollywood, politics and business. The bold-faced names included Oprah Winfrey, Leonardo DiCaprio, Harrison Ford, Michael B. Jordan, Samuel L. Jackson, Spike Lee, Kim Kardashian, Cynthia Erivo, Christoper Nolan. Guillermo Del Toro, Peter Jackson, Denis Villeneuve, Edgar Wright, George R. R. Martin, Nicolas Cage, Doja Cat, Al Pacino, Francis Ford Coppola, Jon M. Chu, Vin Diesel, Gayle King, Katy Perry, Justin Trudeau, Keke Palmer, Jeffrey Katzenberg, Kathleen Kennedy, Frank Marshall, Michael Bloomberg, Bob Iger, Dana Walden, Janelle Monae, Lee Daniels, Ariana Huffington, Tracee Ellis Ross, Zac Posen, Jon Batiste, Diane Warren, California Gov. Gavin Newsom, Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass and former Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi, among many others.
Lucas said he wanted to create a cultural institution that honors illustrators. “When we started this museum, we would sort of tag it as a ‘temple to illustrators,’” he said.
He continued, “I’ve worked with hundreds of illustrators, and I will tell you that they are as talented as any artist I have ever met. This is a way of giving back to them something they’ve all wanted…The illustrators inevitably say the same thing, from R. Crumb to [Norman] Rockwell, they all say the same, ‘I wish I could be in a museum.’”
While Winfrey, Erivo, Kardashian and Rodriguez strolled through the galleries, most of the heavy hitters made their way to the fifth-floor Skywalker Grill restaurant. DiCaprio enjoyed sushi in a banquette with Al Pacino, Andrew Watt and David Furnish. Nolan bent over to say hello to a seated Coppola. Ron Howard and his daughter Bryce Dallas Howard took photos with Kardashian and her boyfriend, car racing champion Lewis Hamilton.
Building the $1.5 billion museum, which was entirely funded by Lucas and Hobson, came with plenty of headaches. In the 20 years since Lucas first proposed the idea, the museum was close to being located in San Francisco and then Chicago. Located in L.A.’s Exposition Park, the Lucas Museum features 1,200 works from Lucas’s 30,000-piece private art collection. Designed by Ma Yansong of MAD Architects, the five-story building, which is frequently described as a “spaceship,” is 300,000 square feet, with 100,000 dedicated to 35 galleries, and sits among a 13-acre campus.
“If your husband or spouse comes home and says they want to build a museum, I suggest your response is a hard no,” Hobson cracked.
She addressed critics who turn their noses up at illustrators. “If critics say a museum of narrative art is too much like a popcorn movie and not enough like an art film, well, we like popcorn movies in our family,” Hobson said to applause. “In fact, we love them.”
The opening night co-chairs included Julie Bell, Guillermo del Toro, Greta Gerwig, Sir Lewis Hamilton, JR, Steven Spielberg and Pharrell Williams. They all stood on stage as Queen Latifah emceed the opening remarks.
“I’m not pinching myself because I felt all the energy and pain of birthing it with George,” Hobson told me on the arrivals red carpet. “I still have a feeling of disbelief. How do we have a museum? It doesn’t quite make sense. Who thinks they’re ever going to say, ‘Come to my museum?’ And you especially don’t do that if you’re me and you’re the youngest of six kids of a single mom in Chicago. That in and of itself is a story. And those are the kinds of stories that are reflected on the walls of the museum.”
As the well-heeled crowd gathered in the lobby for the evening’s introduction, Latifah played cheerleader. “Paris has the Louvre, New York has the Met, and now L.A. has its artistic equal – the Lucas,” she said to cheers and applause.
And with that comes inspiration. Erivo zeroed in on “The Huntress (Lenda),” Julie Bell’s 1996 oil painting of eight-time Ms. Olympia winner Lenda Murray depicted as the Roman goddess of the hunt, Diana. Snapping a photo of the fantasy portrait, Erivo smiled, “We have to make a TV series about her.”
The evening’s program included a drone show narrated by Winfrey and Jackson and a performance by the Black Eyed Peas.
The museum opens to the public on Sept. 22.

title: New Photos of Hayden Panettiere's Memorial Show Connie Britton, Ruby Rose & More Celebs Mourning
description:
Hayden Panettiere
                          New Photos Show Celebs Paying Their Respects ...
body:
Hayden Panettiere
                          New Photos Show Celebs Paying Their Respects ...
                          At Celebration of Life
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 20, 2026
                            10:30 AM PDT
                                                                            
              
    
            Hayden Panettiere's family and famous friends showed up in droves to celebrate her life ... and we have the pics of the memorial.
      
    
            In photos obtained by TMZ ... mourners gathered at the Malibu Pacific Church Saturday evening, including the likes of Connie Britton, Beverly D’Angelo, Evan Ross, Cameron Richardson, Storm Santos and Caroline D'Amore.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Hayden's "Nashville" costar Jonathan Jackson was also in attendance ... and shared a somber with his other costar Sam Palladio who comforted him as he cried.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Also among the crowd was Ruby Rose -- who opened up about losing her "best friend" last week.
      
    
            And we're told ... Hayden’s dad, Skip, wore a suit with Hawaiian-style lei flowers around his neck.
      
    
            Sources previously told TMZ ... around 150 guests showed up to the late actress' church memorial in Malibu, California ... and it was "beautiful."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            "Nashville" alumni Britton and Charles Esten delivered speeches, and Charles performed one of Hayden's songs from the show with a band's accompaniment.
      
    
            We broke the story ... Hayden died August 16 after she was found unresponsive inside a Greenville, South Carolina Airbnb.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Her boyfriend Brian Hickerson was asleep when his brother Zach arrived to find Hayden unresponsive inside and called 911. First responders were unable to revive her.
      
    
            Narcan was found inside the rental ... and Zach later told TMZ Brian administered it after they discovered Hayden unconscious.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            TMZ broke the story ... law enforcement sources believe Hayden died after taking a black-market oxycodone pill laced with fentanyl.
      
    
            We're told Hayden had a longtime drug dealer in Los Angeles who supplied her with prescription pills ... and authorities believe she took an oxy the morning she died.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Hayden's neighbor Mia Terrazas told us on "TMZ Live" a man she suspected was a drug dealer showed up at Hayden's West Hollywood home just days before the South Carolina trip ... carrying a small bag with "Brian" written on it.
      
    
            The investigation has since zeroed in on Hayden's drug source.
      
    
            The DEA searched Hayden's L.A. home nine days after her death for drugs and other evidence ... and sources tell TMZ years of text messages between Hayden and the dealer have become a major focus of the probe.

title: Hayden Panettiere Remembered by Hollywood Celebs During 'Emotional' Memorial
description:
Hayden Panettiere
                          Celebs Honor Late Actress At Malibu Memorial ...
body:
Hayden Panettiere
                          Celebs Honor Late Actress At Malibu Memorial ...
                          Paris Hilton, Connie Britton, Evan Ross & More
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 20, 2026
                            5:25 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 20, 2026
                                9:38 AM PDT
                                    
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Hayden Panettiere was remembered Saturday during a special celebration of life ceremony by some of her closest Hollywood friends -- and we're told the memorial was "emotional and beautiful."
      
    
            Sources with direct knowledge tell TMZ ... celebrities such as Paris Hilton, Evan Ross, Connie Britton, Charles Esten, Lennon Stella and Jonathan Jackson were among the 150 or so guests on hand to honor the late actress at the church memorial in Malibu, California.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            As everyone knows ... Hayden died August 16 after she was found unresponsive inside a Greenville, South Carolina, Airbnb. TMZ broke the story ... law enforcement sources believe Hayden died after taking a black-market oxycodone pill laced with fentanyl.
      

            During Saturday's memorial, Britton and Esten gave speeches, and Esten also sang one of Hayden's songs from their show, "Nashville," with a band set up at the church, our sources say.
      
    
            We're also told the guests watched as doves were released outside the church before moving inside for the ceremony.   
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Hayden’s dad, Skip, attended the memorial ... but, as we first reported, Hayden's mom, Lesley Vogel was not invited, along with Hayden's boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, and his brother Zach.
      
    
            Hayden's mom and dad finalized their years-long divorce in 2016. Hayden and Lesley did not see eye-to-eye during the final years of Hayden's life. As for Brian Hickerson, his longtime rocky relationship with Hayden has been well-documented ... including Hickerson's arrests and her restraining order against him.
